subject: Re: DPA — erase evidence, tombstone retention and rollback SLA
messages:
From: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aurumhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Cc: legal@aurumhealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: DPA — requested clarification on tombstone + rollback evidence

Jonas,

Thanks for the chat earlier — Aurum's legal team reviewed Redwood's latest DPA redline and we have two outstanding asks that block our signature: 1) the tombstone retention language (we need to confirm a maximum tombstone period for user-level metadata after primary deletion), and 2) the rollback/restore carveout: if an incident triggers a rollback, we require an auditable chain proving that the original data was re-removed and not left in secondary copies.

Specifically, can Redwood commit to an operational playbook entry that: a) defines max tombstone duration (we suggested 30 days), b) documents the snapshot/backup expiry and verification steps, and c) provides a certifiable proof artifact (log sample + signed attestation) within 30 calendar days after a rollback event?

We attached our annotated redlines for reference. Happy to hop on a short call if helpful — legal are watching the timeline as Aurum is on a tight regulatory go-live in Q4.

Best,
Claire
Senior Counsel, Aurum Health
Attachments: Aurum_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 13:04:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA — requested clarification on tombstone + rollback evidence

Claire — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Looping Naomi (privacy ops) and Ben (security & observability) so we can put concrete operational language into the DPA appendix.

Short answers up front:
- Tombstone period: reasonable to commit to a configurable default of 30 days for user-level metadata, with an option for customers to request a shorter period subject to operational impact. We do need to preserve a short window (default 7 days) for internal retries and compliance holds; that can be surfaced in the appendix.
- Rollback proof: we can provide an attestation package that includes a signed event log, snapshot IDs, and verification checksums for affected objects. Operationally that sits in our retention/forensics pipeline; turnaround of 30 days is achievable for EU customers on an enterprise support plan.

Action items for us: Naomi, Ben — can you draft a concise appendix section that: 1) defines TTL/tombstone semantics and configurable options, 2) enumerates backup/snapshot expiry timelines, and 3) describes the attestations (log sample + signature) and a template for the certificate we would provide? Aim for text we can propose back to Aurum tomorrow.

Claire — if that aligns, I'll route a draft appendix and a short SLA clause for rollback-response times for your counsel to review.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
From: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
To: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 08:52:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA — draft appendix for tombstones + rollback attestations (internal)

Folks — draft below (keeps legal language tight, operational details in appendix + link to playbook). I've kept binding commitments narrow and operational specifics descriptive to avoid promising RTOs that depend on customer plan. Comments inline welcome.

--- DRAFT APPENDIX TEXT (for external review) ---
1) Tombstone retention: Redwood will, by default, place user-deleted objects into a tombstoned state for a maximum of thirty (30) days to allow for idempotent retries and lawful holds. Customers may request a shorter tombstone period; such requests will be implemented subject to operational assessment and may require a plan change. Logs that are required for regulatory audit may be retained longer only when subject to a lawful hold.

2) Backup & snapshot expiry: System snapshots and backup copies that could contain customer data will be retained at most ninety (90) days unless otherwise agreed in writing. Backups are versioned; each backup set includes a unique snapshot ID and SHA256 checksums for verification.

3) Rollback event attestations: In the event of a rollback/restore that impacts customer data, Redwood will provide an attestation package within thirty (30) calendar days for customers on Enterprise support. The package will include:
- Event timeline (UTC) with operation IDs;
- Snapshot IDs and ranges affected;
- Verification checksums and the results of integrity checks;
- A signed attestation by Redwood's Security Officer stating the remediation actions taken and confirming re-erase of any reintroduced data.

Operational note: The attestation will be produced from immutable audit logs and the forensics pipeline. In rare cases where third-party archive/backup vendors are involved, additional time may be required; in such cases Redwood will notify the customer and propose a remediation timeline.

--- end draft ---

Questions for the thread:
- Ben: is 90 days for snapshot retention defensible (ops/infra costs)? If not, propose alternative.
- Marissa: will we be comfortable offering the 30-day attestation turnaround for EU customers under the enterprise plan? We should also include a clause describing what happens if Redwood discovers residual copies during the attestation process (remediation steps + timeline).

Naomi
Privacy & Risk Lead
From: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
To: Claire Dubois <claire.dubois@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Bcc: legal@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 17:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA — erase evidence, tombstone retention and rollback SLA

Claire — following internal review we attached a short DPA appendix and a redline of your submitted document (see attachments). Summary of what we're proposing:

- Tombstone: default 30 days, configurable shorter windows for customers on request; we will mark the appendix to show the operational default and the change request process.
- Snapshots/backups: snapshot retention capped at 90 days; we provide snapshot IDs + SHA256 checksums as part of the attestation package.
- Rollback attestations: for Enterprise customers we will provide an attestation package within 30 calendar days. The package contains the timeline, snapshot IDs, checksums, and a signed attestation. If a third-party vendor is implicated we will notify Aurum and propose a revised schedule (good-faith cooperation).

We added an explicit remediation path: if during attestation Redwood discovers residual copies we will perform an emergency purge, document the steps taken, and provide an updated attestation within an additional 14 calendar days. That additional remediation window is limited to exceptional cases and will be exception-managed.

Next steps: If Aurum's counsel is happy with the appendix text we'll 1) incorporate it into the DPA, and 2) sign a short addendum that references the Enterprise support plan (AUR-4721) which governs the 30-day attestation commitment. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk legal through the mechanics and sample attestations.

Best regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
